chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Yazeed, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When Allah the Exalted caused Adam to descend, he began patching [his body] with leaves of Paradise, and the garment that was upon him from the garments of Paradise flew off from him. So he picked up a leaf and covered his nakedness with it. When he descended, the aroma of that leaf remained in India with the vegetation. Thus, the perfume came to be in the earth from the cause of that leaf upon which remained the aroma of Paradise. From there, the perfume is in India, because the south wind fell upon the leaf, so its aroma led to the west because it carried the aroma of the leaf in the atmosphere. When the wind stagnated in India, it remained in their trees and their vegetation. The first animal that grazed from that leaf was the musk deer. From there, the musk came to be in the navel of the deer, because the aroma of the vegetation flowed in its body and in its blood, until it gathered in the navel of the deer.
ai.seo_question: What is the origin of musk and perfume according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narrative linking Adam’s physical descent to the material origins of scent, illustrating the Shia concept of the tangible connection between Paradise and Earth. The hadith details how the leaf Adam used to cover his nakedness carried the fragrance of Paradise to India, influencing local flora and fauna, specifically resulting in musk accumulating in the navel of the deer. This account serves as a cosmological explanation for the presence of precious aromatics in the natural world, rooted in the immediate aftermath of the Fall.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad, from Salih Bin Abu Hammad, from Al Husayn Bin Yazeed, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Abu Hamza, 
(It has been narrated) from Ibrahim, from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the Exalted Caused Adam<sup>as</sup> to descend from the Paradise, he<sup>as</sup> started covering himself<sup>as</sup> from a leaf of the Paradise, and his<sup>as</sup> clothes flew away from him<sup>as</sup>, which used to be upon him<sup>as</sup> from the garments of the Paradise. So he<sup>as</sup> cut off a leaf and veiled his<sup>as</sup> nakedness with it. 
So when he<sup>as</sup> descended, the aroma of that leaf remained at India with the vegetation. So the perfume came to be in the earth from the cause of that leaf upon which remained the aroma of the Paradise. Thus, from here on the perfume is at India, because upon the leaf fell the south wind, so its aroma led to the west because it carried the aroma of the leaf in the atmosphere. So when the wind stagnated at India, it remained in its trees, and its vegetation. So the first animal which grazed the musk from that leaf was a deer. Thus, from over there the musk came to be in the navel of the deer flowing the aroma of the vegetation in its body, and in its blood, gathering in the navel of the deer’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Muhammad from Salih ibn abu Hammad from al-Husayn ibn Yazid from al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn abu Hamzah from Ibrahim who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

when Allah sent Adam, Alayhi al-Salam, down, he began to hold the leaves of the garden (paradises) to himself, and his clothes which were of the dresses of the garden (paradises) that he wore flew away from him. He picked up a leaf to cover his private parts. When he came down the perfume of that leaf trapped in India; the wind from the south blew and its perfume reached to the west. It carried the perfume of the leaf in the air. When the wind became stagnant in India, it adhered to its trees and their plants. The first animal that grazed on such a plant was a deer of musk and from that is musk in the bellybutton of the deer; the fragrance of the plant moved in her body and blood until it gathered in the bellybutton of the deer.’”
